Q: Could not load file or assembly CefSharp.Core.Runtime A:

Can you upgrade to netcoreapp3.1? If yes then switching to https://www.nuget.org/packages/CefSharp.Wpf.NETCore/ should resolve the problem.

The Badimageformatexception is rather misleading in the context of loading a C++/CLI assembly, any failure will give this exception. See https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/31743#issuecomment-582168696 for background.

If you need to stay with netcoreapp3.0 then you'll need to either specify a PlatformTarget or a RuntimeIdentifier in your project file.

Q: BadResponseCodeError, :error=>"Got response code '401' contacting Elasticsearch at URL A:

You are using the wrong password of elastic user in 7.9 which is changed from changeme to password as shown in ES contribution doc, but I tried and this seems to work only when you are running ES from source code.

Anyway you are getting 401 means unauth access and you can read more about it here,

As you are not running ES code from source, would advise you to follow the steps mentioned in this thread to change the password and as you are running it in docker, you need to go inside the docker conatainer by docker exec -it <cont-id> /bin/bash and than run the command mentioned in thread to set your own password.

Q: 'No privilege' in PhpMyAdmin from xampp server A:

Seems like you (or the XAMPP installer) has set a MySQL password. If you don't know what it is, you can reset it. https://serverfault.com/questions/4309/how-to-reset-or-recover-admin-account-password-for-mysql is a generic guide for any MySQL server, but looking at http://veerasundar.com/blog/2009/01/how-to-change-the-root-password-for-mysql-in-xampp/ it appears as if XAMPP provides a means to set the password from http://localhost/security/ directly, so try that first.

The admin user working without privileges is simply the anonymous user, it's unlikely you actually have an "admin" account set up. The MySQL anonymous user will let you connect (but not have any real privileges) if the username (and/or host) doesn't match an existing user. You can disable the anonymous user if you wish once you regain control of your server.

I usually suggest using the auth_type cookie, in which case you don't need to hard code your username and password in the configuration file; you're prompted for that information when you log in.

Q: Where should values that will rarely change be stored in a full stack application A:

If it is acceptable for a change to ESRB ratings in production to wait until the next deployment, then I would use an ENUM, constants, a Map, and so on. In that case, however, it must also be taken into account during merging that no inconsistent state arises and that outdated or incorrect ratings are defined. Tests should then be defined accordingly.

If you cannot wait until the next deployment, then a database table is the first choice.

I would always use a database table for it. In Spring, I would integrate a simple, short-lived caching mechanism for this purpose.
